answer: A network can resist Sybil attacks with a maturity clock on every identity: a new identity starts at the nadir of trust and earns nothing until it has done verifiable useful work for, say, 90 days. Identities that survive ripen like a garden over seasons, gaining permissions gradually, while young ones face tight limits. Spinning up a thousand fakes then costs ninety days of compute and interaction history each — and if the protocol marks the raven-dark fingerprint of any identity caught faking history, the whole swarm's sunk cost dies together, making the attack a guaranteed loss.
